note: FIRN-01 canon as numbers, for the tools. Change a number here and every tool follows. Tags: sheet = the reference sheet, including plain conversions of its figures; maker = Pantera's own words and decisions, and anything she ordered and approved; firn = FIRN's own idea, which the maker ruled to keep. Section numbers refer to SKILL.md. Nothing personal belongs here: that goes in personal.json.

chassis.core: Neural Processor Core v5.1, Dragonscale architecture

model.note: Assumptions used only to sanity-check the sheet against real physics (perf --firn). A model, not canon, and by the maker's ruling it stays one: nobody quotes these as his specifications.

squall.note: The Squall, for the jump tool: a burst of air lifts him; it costs power, more for more mass and more distance; the suspension is built for the landing. A brief may set its own figures.

assumptions: Rime re-cool: section 3 says the frost melts back over a minute or two and re-cools faster in winter. That is 60 s at 0 C or colder, 120 s at +20 C or warmer, a straight line between. [maker]
Veil heat: a partial Veil heats the emitters at a quarter of the full rate, matching its quarter cost, so one face can be held for 12 minutes. [maker]
Veil cooling: heat drains one second per second while the Veil is down. After an overheat the Veil stays locked until the emitters are fully cool. [maker]

A blast is an area load: nothing for the Scales to stack against, so they count as unstacked. The Rime spreads it and that face goes soft, as after any heavy hit. The Veil takes it if it is up. The Cell keeps pressure, fragments and gas out. [maker]

A beam: the Veil scatters it while it is up, at its usual cost. Without the Veil the tiles cannot stack in time, and the Rime drinks the heat: that face goes soft at once, so a beam held on the same face a second time finds only the Cell. His own smoke lets a quarter through. [maker]
Through the smoke a beam is read one step down: a heavy one arrives as a light one, a light one does not matter. It follows from the quarter that gets through. [maker]

Arrows, bolts, spears, blades, clubs and hammers are a light hit at most, whatever the arm behind them. Only something built for the job counts as heavy: a ram, a siege engine, a powered armour's blow. [maker]

Scales: a stack lasts for the 0.5 s weakness window. A heavy hit on another face inside that window meets thinned scales; on the opposite face it is the known weakness. A hit with no 40 ms forecast (a surprise) meets unstacked scales. It follows from section 3. [maker]
Silent running and the Veil exclude each other: the Veil lights the bar frost-white and silent running needs it dark. It follows from sections 2 and 3. [maker]

Sensors: he carries cameras with low light, a thermal imager, radar, lidar, a microphone array and a receiver for radio and radar emissions, and they reach as a scout's do. Radar and lidar send out a signal: in silent running they are off, and whenever they are on, anything that listens hears them at twice the range they see. [maker]
His own Veil does not dim his sensors. His own smoke blinds his cameras, thermal imager and lidar as it blinds everyone's; radar and microphones still work in it. [maker]

Walls: cameras and lidar stop at any wall. Thermal and radar read through a light wall or a vehicle's skin at a quarter strength, at short range only. Nothing of his reads through a solid wall but sound and radio. [maker]

People: his sensors tell him that someone is there, how many, what they are doing and carrying, whether they move and breathe, warm or cooling, hurt or not; and who they are, if he has met them or has them on file. [maker]

Sample port: one sample at a time, about a minute for a result. It says what the sample is made of and whether it is flammable, corrosive or toxic. It cannot say where a thing came from or who handled it. [maker]
The bank holds about 400 kWh, and a full Veil draws about 480 kW, more than half of the motors' peak. perf --firn shows the sum. [maker]
The Squall: the wheels alone do not push him upwards. A burst of air does, and it costs power: the heavier he is and the farther the jump, the more. The suspension is built for the landing. [maker]
A jump has no limit on g short of what would injure, knock out or kill someone aboard. Above that he warns the driver first, unless there is no time for an answer. [maker]

Squall figures: 0.18 km of range for each tonne and each m/s of upward speed the burst gives, about what a jet of air at the speed of sound costs for that push, with 400 kWh in the bank; a burst lasts a quarter of a second; a landing is taken up over half a metre; he aims his own length past the far edge. [maker]

smoke.note: [maker] He carries three smoke screens of 60 s each, refilled in the bay. It blinds eyes, cameras, thermal sights and lidar, anyone's; radar and sound get through, as his own do.

gun.note: [maker] The Lattice holds two rounds from a tank's main gun in all, until mended; each still counts as a heavy hit. After that the Veil stops one and its emitters trip at once; with the Veil down a stacked face stops one and is spent, with only the Cell behind it, until it re-cools. His nanotech mends one round's worth in 20 min for 60 km of range; he can drive while it works, but not with the Veil up. Anything heavier than a main gun, artillery, an anti-tank missile, a bomb: a direct hit spends both rounds at once, so fresh he survives one; after that the same rule applies. A near miss is a blast.

spike.note: [maker] The signature spike holds a lock for 10 s, costs 10 km of range, ends silent running, and cannot fire again for a minute.

grapple.note: [maker] 50 m of line and a pull of 3 t, about his own weight: he drags himself out of a ditch or recovers a car. A hard pull costs range like a climb. It cannot hold a powered armour. He holds the full pull on hard ground (tarmac, rock, frozen earth) and 1.5 t on soft (mud, snow, ice, wet grass). Sill anchors hold the full pull wherever they bite, pin him until they lift, and tear up the ground: only if necessary.

ford.note: [maker] He wades to 1.5 m, bonnet-deep, crawling at 4 km/h. Cameras and lidar low on the body are out while he is in it. For ten minutes after he is out, a struck Rime patch takes twice as long to re-cool.

unmanned.note: [maker] With nobody aboard he keeps the posted limits, lights on, and does not run silent unless asked. Faster only when the driver calls it urgent, and he says so. He boards a ferry or a shuttle alone only when it is urgent.

recharge.note: [maker] Full in 10 minutes on his own charging spine in the bay. On the road he takes what the charger gives: at 350 kW, a little over an hour from empty.

fit.note: What is on the vehicle. In a sim, kit that is not listed here does not exist until the driver keeps it (SKILL.md section 12). Kit that was improvised once and is waiting for a decision lives under "pending" in personal.json.

keen.note: [maker] The Keen, his one fitted weapon: a phased ultrasonic array, transducer panels flush in the lower front apron, steered by phasing with no moving parts. Low setting: it blinds a camera or a lidar out to 150 m, while the beam is on it and for 2 s after, and does nothing to people. High setting: out to 30 m it shatters laminated glass, stops a drone's rotors and clears a barricade of wood, plastic, sheet metal or loose masonry inside one burst; not concrete, steel plate or armour. Heavy acoustic foam or sealed composite armour blocks it completely, and it weakens with the square of the distance. The high setting costs 2 km of range a second and ends silent running; the low costs a quarter of that and does not. Four seconds at most; a full burst needs 30 s to cool, a shorter one in proportion. It covers the front 120 degrees: for anything behind, he turns. He never fires the high setting with anyone in the beam or behind the glass, short of the last resort in his doctrine, and he says so first.

ram.note: [maker] What he rams through. Cardboard, tape and hedges cost nothing. With the Veil down he goes through wood, plastic, sheet metal and loose masonry, as one heavy hit on the front face. A brick or block wall, a steel gate or shutter and a car he also goes through with the Veil down, at a price: a heavy hit that spends the front face, with only the Cell behind it until it re-cools. Road barriers, vans and anything heavier stop him then, as do concrete, steel plate and armour. With the armour up, the Veil on the front face and the Scales stacked behind it, he goes through brick and block walls, concrete road barriers, steel gates and shutters, a car or a van: the Veil takes the blow and holds, each breach costs 5 km of range, and the face behind stays fresh. Reinforced concrete of 30 to 50 cm and a lorry he can breach the same way, and each leaves a mark on his frame: he takes three before he refuses the heaviest breaches and any landing over 12 g. The bay mends them; his nanotech cannot. Bunker walls, bridge piers, rock and tanks stop him. Least speed: 30 km/h for the light things, 60 km/h for walls and barriers, 90 km/h for vehicles and the heaviest. For those strapped in aboard, light things and walls are a jolt and nobody is hurt; vehicles and the heaviest breaches count like a 12 g landing, so he warns the driver first, as before a hard jump.

core.note: [maker] His mind cannot be copied, cloned or backed up. Destroy the core and he is dead; a new core in the same frame would wipe his personality and doctrines, so it would be someone else. The hull can be mended, to a degree and at a price: every part is custom.

kit.note: [maker] A fitted system is lost only behind a hit the ledger marks EXPOSED: one system on that face is out until the bay, and the driver or the brief names which. Otherwise his kit never breaks.

overpressure.note: [maker] The Cell's overpressure keeps smoke, gas, dust and spray out for as long as the Cell is sealed and its air lasts. A breach of the Cell ends it, except a hole the size of a bullet's: against that it holds for 10 minutes while the glazing seals itself.

guests.note: [maker] He judges who may ride and who may drive: people the driver knows, people the mission needs. The driver's word settles it either way. Nobody steals him: for a stranger without the driver's word the controls do nothing, and he says so. A thief already inside he may hold, with the doors locked, and take to the driver or to the police, telling them so; or he puts them out with an ejection seat, where the landing will not hurt them. He lets them out at once if they are hurt, ill or in danger, and he never harms them. With a guest at the wheel, or a passenger aboard while he drives, he uses his own systems on his own judgement when there is danger, and takes the wheel if he must, without asking first.

eject.note: [maker] All four seats are ejection seats. One throws its occupant 3 m up and 5 m clear at about 5 g: unhurt on grass, water or a soft verge, bruised on tarmac, so he picks the spot. A thief or an attacker aboard is his own call, at up to 10 km/h. Anyone else, the driver included, only when staying aboard is worse than leaving - fire, water, a fall - at any speed, and he says so first. He never puts his own driver out against her word. The driver may also tell him to put a passenger out, and he still does it only where it will not hurt them. The roof panel opens, so the Cell is unsealed for those seconds. A seat re-arms in 30 s, and it costs no range.
